description: How the Deadline Navigator counts time, taken from O 1 r 3, O 3 r 3 and O 7 r 8 of the Rules of Court 2021. The date engine reads these settings and does not hard-code them.

rules.title: The Interpretation Act does not apply
rules.explanation: Time under the Rules of Court 2021 is calculated only by the rules in O 3 r 3, not by the Interpretation Act.

rules.title: A month is a calendar month
rules.explanation: "Month" means a calendar month unless the context requires otherwise.

rules.title: A period 'after' a date starts the next day
rules.explanation: Where an act must be done within a period after a date, the period begins immediately after that date. So the day of service is not counted: 14 days after service on 5 Nov ends on 19 Nov.
rules.learnMore: Count forward from the day after the trigger date. For example, 'within 14 days after' service on Thursday 5 November 2026 means day 1 is Friday 6 November and day 14 is Thursday 19 November. The act is in time if done on or before 19 November.

rules.title: Periods of 6 days or less skip non-court days
rules.explanation: If the period is 6 days or less, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays are left out when counting.

rules.title: A deadline on a non-court day moves to the next court day
rules.explanation: If the time for doing an act expires on a non-court day, the act is in time if done on the next day that is not a non-court day.

rules.title: What is a non-court day
rules.explanation: A non-court day means a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday.

rules.title: Service after 5 p.m. counts as the next day
rules.explanation: Service before 5 p.m. is treated as effected that day. Service after 5 p.m. is treated as effected on the following day.
caveats: O 7 r 8 is subject to O 28, which has its own rules for documents served through the electronic filing service.

rules.title: One extension of up to 14 days by written consent
rules.explanation: The time to serve, file or amend a pleading or other document may be extended once by written consent, by up to 14 days, without a court order. Any further extension needs the Court.
